column1: # Gen 1 -> gen 2 test parity manifest (iemmixer #25; parity report section 7, rule 4).
# One row per test of the predecessor zbynekdrlik/reaperiem at 03be5b97deafdc5d765516014c3f59370edd534b:
# 543 Rust test functions, 276 Playwright tests (snapshot-isolation runs one body for two member pairs: two rows), 89 Python tests.
# gen1_file and gen1_test are the predecessor's names, scrubbed of site data (P6) with scripts/scrub_import.py;
# a #N inside a gen 1 name is the predecessor's reaperiem#N.
# status: PORTED (the same test is in gen 2), TRANSFORMED (another gen 2 test checks the same behaviour),
# OBSOLETE (a REAPER-only mechanism removed by design; the reason says why), PENDING (no gen 2 test yet),
# FEATURE-GAP (the behaviour is missing in gen 2).
# gen2: 'path::test' refs separated by '; ' - a Rust test fn name, a Playwright test title exactly as written,
# scripts/check_parity_manifest.py checks every row in CI. PENDING or FEATURE-GAP is allowed only while the reason
# names 'S7 #10' or 'S6 #9'; S8 #11 runs it with --cutover, which allows none.
# A removed or renamed gen 2 test updates its refs here; a row is never deleted.

secrets moved into write-once files and the site file rejects secret keys
gen2 has no config-merge: install-site replaces the whole site file via state::write_atomic, so there is no per-key merge to no-op; rewriting the same site leaves it byte-identical
state::write_atomic renames a temp file over the site; no .tmp sibling survives (S6 #9 F30 install-site)
a write that fails at its temp file (before the rename, before any byte of the site is touched) leaves the original site byte-for-byte (S6 #9 F30 install-site)
